claims.text: Equiatomic FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt alloys exhibit soft ferromagnetism with low coercivity.
The proposed starting FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt alloy is an fcc high-entropy alloy with configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Controlled interstitial nitrogen doping can increase coercivity in an equiatomic FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy.
A nitrogen-rich atmosphere and elevated synthesis temperature can incorporate nitrogen interstitially without causing phase separation.
Nitrogen atoms occupy interstitial sites in the fcc lattice.
Interstitial nitrogen induces localized lattice distortions.
Interstitial nitrogen may create locally tetragonal regions.
Nitrogen-induced lattice distortion enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Nitrogen-induced lattice distortion creates additional magnetic-domain pinning sites.
Enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy and additional domain pinning increase coercivity.
Relevant lattice distortions are less pronounced in the undoped Pd- and Pt-containing baseline alloys.
Nitrogen-doped FeCoNi-based alloy will have higher coercivity than FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt baselines.
Nitrogen-doped FeCoNi-based alloy will retain high saturation magnetization.
The coercivity benefit requires homogeneous incorporation of a moderate amount of nitrogen.
Excessive nitrogen may cause phase segregation or nitride precipitation.
Phase segregation or nitride precipitation may undermine high-entropy-alloy characteristics or degrade magnetic performance.

contradictions.description: The initial host is specified as a Pd- or Pt-containing quaternary alloy, whereas the experiment calls for nitrogen-doped equiatomic FeCoNi samples and compares them against quaternary FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt. Thus the experiment changes both nitrogen content and host composition rather than clearly testing nitrogen addition to the stated initial alloy.
